global.description: Values shared by every workload, hook and cronjob: image registry, pull secrets, common labels and annotations.

nameOverride.description: Replaces the chart name in the fullname and in app.kubernetes.io/name. A DNS-1123 subdomain, the loosest name it reaches; the stricter labels it can reach are checked at render time, where the release name is visible (issue #120). The empty string means no override.

fullnameOverride.description: Replaces the fullname that heads every generated name. A DNS-1123 subdomain, the loosest name it reaches; the stricter labels it can reach are checked at render time, where the release name is visible (issue #120). The empty string means no override.

workloads.description: The workloads of the release, keyed by name. Each entry renders a Deployment, or a StatefulSet with kind: StatefulSet, with its Service, ServiceAccount, ConfigMap, Secret, HPA, PDB and NetworkPolicy, named <fullname>-<key>.

ingress.description: The single Ingress of the release, rendered when enabled. Part of the HTTP routing layer: it excludes httpRoute and httpRoutes.

httpRoute.description: The single HTTPRoute of the release (Gateway API), rendered when enabled. Excludes ingress; coexists with httpRoutes.

httpRoutes.description: HTTPRoutes keyed by name, each rendered as <fullname>-<key> (issue #195). An entry present is a route rendered. Excludes ingress; coexists with httpRoute.

tcpRoutes.description: TCPRoutes keyed by name, each rendered as <fullname>-<key>: L4 routes for raw TCP ports on an existing Gateway listener. Needs gateway.networking.k8s.io/v1 TCPRoute (Gateway API v1.6.0 or later).

udpRoutes.description: UDPRoutes keyed by name, each rendered as <fullname>-<key>: the same shape as tcpRoutes, for UDP ports. Needs gateway.networking.k8s.io/v1 UDPRoute (Gateway API v1.6.0 or later).

cronJobs.description: Root-scope CronJobs keyed by name. They inherit nothing from a workload: set image, or fromWorkload to run a workload's image. A cronjob under workloads.<name>.cronJobs inherits from its workload instead.

hooks.description: Root-scope Helm hooks: hooks.<hook type>.<name>, each a Job run at that phase. They inherit nothing from a workload: set image, or fromWorkload to run a workload's image. A hook under workloads.<name>.hooks inherits from its workload instead.

externalSecrets.description: ExternalSecrets keyed by name, each rendered as one ExternalSecret (External Secrets Operator). Workloads and jobs read the Secret it produces through their own externalSecrets list, by this key.

kedaTriggerAuthentications.description: KEDA TriggerAuthentications keyed by name, each rendered as <fullname>-<key>. A trigger's authenticationRef.name that is a key here resolves to the rendered name.

defaults.description: Fallbacks for hooks and cronjobs of both scopes.

rbacs.description: Roles, RoleBindings and ServiceAccounts the release creates.

imagePullSecret.description: A pull secret by name: a string, or a map with only name.

name.description: Name of an existing image pull Secret in the release namespace.

imageRegistry.description: Registry host, with optional port and path, prepended to every image whose first segment is not already a registry. A host carries a "." or a ":" port, or is localhost: the same test imageString applies. Never a URL.

imagePullSecrets.description: Pull secrets of a pod that sets no imagePullSecrets key, when neither does the workload a workload-scope job belongs to.

commonLabels.description: Labels added to metadata.labels of every resource, never to the selector labels. The chart's own app.kubernetes.io/* and helm.sh/chart labels win over them, and a per-resource label (podLabels) wins over both.

commonAnnotations.description: Annotations added to metadata.annotations of every resource, pod templates included. A per-resource annotation of the same name wins, the empty string included. helm.sh/hook, helm.sh/hook-weight and helm.sh/hook-delete-policy here are dropped: the chart emits those itself.

image.$comment: The host, path-component, tag and digest fragments are repeated in the patterns of the string branch, imageMap's repository, tag (its @<digest> suffix included) and digest, and global.imageRegistry: JSON Schema cannot compose patterns, so change them together. The host alternative mirrors the registry test in imageString (_image-helpers.tpl).

oneOf.description: Full image reference, e.g. nginx:1.25, held to the reference grammar the kubelet parses: [host/]path[:tag][@digest], lowercase path components. A host carries a "." or a ":" port, or is localhost, the same test imageString applies. A reference outside it rendered and then failed at pull time with InvalidImageName. IPv6 registry hosts are not accepted.

repository.description: [registry[:port]/]path, lowercase path components; no tag or digest, which have their own fields.

tag.description: An OCI tag: up to 128 characters of [A-Za-z0-9_.-], not starting with . or -, optionally followed by @<digest> (ADR 0018): the form Argo CD Image Updater writes with the digest strategy (GetTagWithDigest()), since its Helm target has no digest key. Rendered as written, repo:<tag>@<digest>; a digest here rules out image.digest. Quote a numeric-looking tag: YAML reads a bare 1.20 as the number 1.2, which no template can turn back into 1.20.

digest.description: A digest as the kubelet parses it (distribution/reference): <algorithm>:<hex>, at least 32 hex characters, e.g. sha256:<64 hex>. Wins over a plain tag when both are set; together with a tag that carries its own @<digest> it is rejected, even when the two are equal (ADR 0018).

pullPolicy.description: The container's imagePullPolicy; IfNotPresent when unset. A job running this image takes it with the image, unless it sets imagePullPolicy.

imageMap.$comment: A tag carrying @<digest> and a non-empty digest are two sources for one pin: digest would win and drop the tag's in silence (ADR 0018). imageString rejects the pair too, for --skip-schema-validation.

then.$comment: Not false: a false schema reports only "false schema" at the image, maxLength 0 points the error at /digest.

requests.description: Resource requests of the container, rendered verbatim: Kubernetes quantities, such as cpu: 100m and memory: 128Mi.

cpu.description: CPU request: a Kubernetes quantity, such as 100m or 0.5.

memory.description: Memory request: a Kubernetes quantity, such as 128Mi.

limits.description: Resource limits of the container, rendered verbatim: Kubernetes quantities.

cpu.description: CPU limit: a Kubernetes quantity, such as 500m or 1.

memory.description: Memory limit: a Kubernetes quantity, such as 512Mi. A container above it is OOM-killed.

claims.description: Dynamic resource claims of the container (Kubernetes DRA), rendered verbatim: each names an entry of the pod's resourceClaims.

name.description: Name of a resource claim of the pod.

volumes.description: Kubernetes volumes, each a native volume source. Open: about thirty volume sources, and the list grows (ADR 0017). Each item declares the fields a template reads: name (renderVolume and the externalSecrets volume collision check) and the keys removed in 4.0.0 that renderVolume rejects naming their replacement (ADR 0022).

name.description: Name of the pod volume, which a volumeMounts item mounts. Unique within the pod, generated volumes included.

type.description: removed in 4.0.0, issue #183: write the native volume source.

secret.description: A native secret volume source, rendered verbatim.

name.description: removed in 4.0.0, issue #183: use secret.secretName.

persistentVolumeClaim.description: A native persistentVolumeClaim volume source, rendered verbatim.

name.description: removed in 4.0.0, issue #183: use persistentVolumeClaim.claimName.

volumeMounts.description: Kubernetes volumeMounts of the main container. Open: a passthrough surface that grows with Kubernetes (ADR 0017). Each item declares the fields a template reads: mountPath (validateMountPaths, the duplicate mountPath check) and name, which Kubernetes requires beside it.

name.description: Name of the pod volume to mount.

mountPath.description: Path in the container. Unique within the container, the mounts the chart generates included.

probe.description: Kubernetes probe configuration (httpGet, tcpSocket, exec, grpc). Closed in full, handler bodies included: a small, fixed shape (ADR 0017). The rule "exactly one handler" stays with the API server.

exec.description: Run a command in the container: healthy when it exits 0.

command.description: The command and its arguments, run without a shell: wrap it in ["sh", "-c", ...] for one.

httpGet.description: An HTTP GET against the container: healthy on a status from 200 to 399.

host.description: Host to connect to; the pod IP when unset. To set the Host header, use httpHeaders.

path.description: Path of the request, such as /healthz.

port.description: Port to probe: a number, or the name of a container port.

scheme.description: HTTP (the default) or HTTPS. HTTPS skips certificate verification.

name.description: Header name.

tcpSocket.description: Open a TCP connection to the container: healthy when it connects.

host.description: Host to connect to; the pod IP when unset.

port.description: Port to probe: a number, or the name of a container port.

grpc.description: A gRPC health check (grpc.health.v1) against the container.

port.description: Port of the gRPC server, a number: a port name is not accepted here.

service.description: Service name sent in the health check request; empty checks the server as a whole.

initialDelaySeconds.description: Seconds after the container starts before the first probe. Kubernetes defaults to 0.

periodSeconds.description: Seconds between probes. Kubernetes defaults to 10.

timeoutSeconds.description: Seconds before a probe times out. Kubernetes defaults to 1.

successThreshold.description: Consecutive successes to count as healthy after a failure. Kubernetes defaults to 1, and requires 1 for a liveness or startup probe.

failureThreshold.description: Consecutive failures to count as unhealthy. Kubernetes defaults to 3.

terminationGracePeriodSeconds.description: Grace period after a failed liveness or startup probe kills the container, overriding the pod's terminationGracePeriodSeconds.

create.description: Create the ServiceAccount. Defaults to true for a workload and an rbacs.roles entry. A hook or cronjob creates one by default only when nothing else names a ServiceAccount for it: not its own name, not its workload's.

automount.description: automountServiceAccountToken of the ServiceAccount itself; true when unset, after a job's own automountServiceAccountToken. A pod-level automountServiceAccountToken wins over it at admission.

annotations.description: Annotations on the ServiceAccount, such as eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn, merged over global.commonAnnotations.

name.description: ServiceAccount name: a DNS-1123 subdomain of at most 253 characters. The empty string means the scope's default name.

enabled.description: Render the workload's Service; true when unset. false drops it, and an ingress or route backend naming the workload fails the render. A StatefulSet keeps its headless Service either way.

portName.description: Name of the primary port, on the Service and the container; "http" when unset. A route or ingress backend picks a port by this name.

port.description: Port the Service exposes for the primary port; 80 when unset.

targetPort.description: The pod port the primary port forwards to: a number, which becomes the container's declared port, or the name of a declared container port. Defaults to portName, with the container port then equal to port. A name no container port declares fails the render.

protocol.description: Protocol of the primary port: TCP (the default), UDP or SCTP.

annotations.description: Annotations on the Service, such as for external-dns or a cloud load balancer, merged over global.commonAnnotations. Not copied onto a StatefulSet's headless Service.

extraPorts.description: More ports of the same Service, after the primary one. Names and port+protocol pairs are unique across the primary port and every entry. A numeric targetPort is also declared on the container, under the entry's name, unless the container already declares that number and protocol.

name.description: Port name, on the Service and, for a numeric targetPort, on the container.

targetPort.description: The pod port it forwards to: a number, declared on the container under the entry's name unless that number and protocol already are, or the name of a declared container port.

appProtocol.description: The port's appProtocol, rendered verbatim, such as http or kubernetes.io/h2c.

nodePort.description: Fixed node port, in the cluster's default NodePort range: for a NodePort or LoadBalancer Service only. Unset, Kubernetes picks one.

service.description: An empty portName is accepted only while the Service has one port: with extraPorts it is multi-port, and the API server requires every port of a multi-port Service to be named.

hpaTargetPercent.description: 0 or "" turns this metric off. A string holds digits only: "80%" is rejected, and so is a leading zero, which prints unquoted and reads as octal. With enabled: true at least one of the two targets must be positive.

deploymentReloader.description: Opt-in integration with Stakater Reloader (ADR 0016). Inert without Reloader installed.

externalSecrets.description: Render secret.reloader.stakater.com/reload on the workload with the target Secret of every externalSecrets entry it references, env and mounted, so Reloader rolls the pods when ESO rewrites one (value rotation, rollout race). Merged with a reload list set in annotations or global.commonAnnotations. Requires at least one referenced externalSecrets entry.

enabled.description: Renders an autoscaling/v2 HorizontalPodAutoscaler for the workload, which becomes its replica owner: spec.replicas is omitted. The render fails with keda.enabled also true, or when neither target is positive.

minReplicas.description: The HPA's spec.minReplicas. Required when enabled: the render fails without it. The replica owner's floor the pdb check reads.

maxReplicas.description: The HPA's spec.maxReplicas. Required when enabled: the render fails without it.

targetCPUUtilizationPercentage.description: Average CPU utilization, as a percentage of the request, rendered as a Resource metric with target type Utilization.

targetMemoryUtilizationPercentage.description: Average memory utilization, as a percentage of the request, rendered as a Resource metric with target type Utilization.

behavior.description: The HPA's spec.behavior. Only scaleUp and scaleDown are read, each rendered verbatim; any other key is ignored.

enabled.description: Renders the ScaledObject, which becomes the workload's replica owner: spec.replicas is omitted. Requires triggers and the keda.sh/v1alpha1 CRDs; the render fails with autoscaling.enabled also true.

annotations.description: Annotations of the ScaledObject, e.g. autoscaling.keda.sh/paused. Added over global.commonAnnotations; an annotation of the same name here wins.

minReplicaCount.description: Fewest replicas KEDA scales to. Omitted when unset: KEDA's default is 0, the floor the pdb check then reads.

maxReplicaCount.description: Most replicas KEDA scales to. Omitted when unset: KEDA's default is 100.

idleReplicaCount.description: Replicas while no trigger is active; KEDA requires it below minReplicaCount. Omitted when unset.

pollingInterval.description: Seconds between KEDA's checks of each trigger. Omitted when unset: KEDA's default is 30.

cooldownPeriod.description: Seconds after the last trigger reported active before KEDA scales the workload to 0; applies only when minReplicaCount is 0. Omitted when unset: KEDA's default is 300.

initialCooldownPeriod.description: Seconds after the ScaledObject is created before cooldownPeriod applies. Omitted when unset: KEDA's default is 0.

fallback.description: The ScaledObject's spec.fallback: the replicas KEDA keeps while a scaler keeps failing. Rendered verbatim when non-empty.

failureThreshold.description: Consecutive scaler failures before KEDA falls back; rendered verbatim.

replicas.description: Replicas KEDA sets once failureThreshold is reached; rendered verbatim.

behavior.description: How KEDA applies fallback.replicas, e.g. static or currentReplicasIfHigher; rendered verbatim.

advanced.description: The ScaledObject's spec.advanced, rendered verbatim when non-empty.

restoreToOriginalReplicaCount.description: Whether KEDA scales the workload back to its original replica count when the ScaledObject is deleted; rendered verbatim. KEDA's default is false.

horizontalPodAutoscalerConfig.description: Settings of the HPA KEDA derives for the ScaledObject; rendered verbatim.

name.description: Name of the HPA KEDA derives; KEDA uses keda-hpa-<ScaledObject name> when unset. Rendered verbatim.

behavior.description: The derived HPA's spec.behavior (scaleUp, scaleDown); rendered verbatim.

scalingModifiers.description: KEDA scaling modifiers (formula, target, activationTarget, metricType), which combine the triggers by their name; rendered verbatim.

triggers.description: The ScaledObject's triggers, each rendered verbatim but for authenticationRef.name, which resolves a kedaTriggerAuthentications key. Required, non-empty, when enabled: the render fails otherwise, and on a null entry.

key.description: The taint key to tolerate. Empty, with operator Exists, tolerates every taint.

operator.description: Exists or Equal; Kubernetes takes Equal when unset.

value.description: A string, as Toleration.value is: quote a number ("1").

effect.description: The taint effect to tolerate; empty matches every effect.

tolerationSeconds.description: How long a NoExecute taint is tolerated before eviction; unset tolerates it forever. Kubernetes accepts it only with effect NoExecute.

ip.description: The IP address the hostnames resolve to, rendered verbatim as HostAlias.ip.

hostnames.description: The hostnames that resolve to ip, rendered verbatim as HostAlias.hostnames.

name.description: The resolver option's name, such as ndots, rendered verbatim as PodDNSConfigOption.name.

value.description: PodDNSConfigOption.value is a string; a number is printed in digits and quoted by the template (printScalar), so ndots: 2 is accepted.

parameter.description: The scaler's authentication parameter the value fills, e.g. password; rendered verbatim.

name.description: Name of an existing Secret in the release namespace; rendered verbatim, not resolved against externalSecrets.

key.description: Key of the Secret that holds the value; rendered verbatim.

parameter.description: The scaler's authentication parameter the value fills, e.g. password; rendered verbatim.

name.description: The environment variable of the scale target's container that holds the value; rendered verbatim.

containerName.description: The container whose environment variable is read; rendered verbatim. When unset KEDA falls back to scaleTargetRef.envSourceContainerName, which the chart does not set.

container.description: A Kubernetes Container, passed through to the manifest. Open on purpose (ADR 0006): only env is held, to envVar, so a numeric value fails here and not at apply (issue #148), and volumeMounts is declared an array because validateStatefulSets reads it (issue #235), null kept as it passed while undeclared.

env.description: The container's environment variables, each held to envVar, rendered verbatim.

volumeMounts.description: The container's volumeMounts, rendered verbatim. On a StatefulSet's extraContainers and extraInitContainers, their names count as mounts of the volumeClaimTemplates entries (validateStatefulSets).

name.description: The variable's name, rendered verbatim as EnvVar.name.

value.description: A string, as EnvVar.value is: quote a number ("10"), or the API server rejects the manifest.

valueFrom.description: A Kubernetes EnvVarSource (secretKeyRef, configMapKeyRef, fieldRef, resourceFieldRef), rendered verbatim as EnvVar.valueFrom. Exclusive with value.

type.description: The KEDA scaler, e.g. prometheus, cron or rabbitmq; rendered verbatim.

name.description: Name of the trigger, which scalingModifiers formulas refer to; rendered verbatim.

metricType.description: The metric target type of the trigger in the derived HPA; rendered verbatim. KEDA's default is AverageValue.

useCachedMetrics.description: Whether the HPA's metric queries read the value KEDA cached at the last pollingInterval; rendered verbatim. KEDA's default is false.

metadata.description: map[string]string in the ScaledObject: quote a number ("10").

authenticationRef.description: The TriggerAuthentication or ClusterTriggerAuthentication the trigger authenticates with.

name.description: A kedaTriggerAuthentications key resolves to the rendered <fullname>-<key>, and the render fails when that entry is empty; any other name is rendered verbatim, for a TriggerAuthentication outside the chart.

kind.description: TriggerAuthentication, KEDA's default, or ClusterTriggerAuthentication; rendered verbatim. With ClusterTriggerAuthentication, name is never resolved against kedaTriggerAuthentications.

secretTargetRef.description: Values read from Secret keys; spec.secretTargetRef of the TriggerAuthentication, rendered verbatim when non-empty.

env.description: Values read from environment variables of the scale target's containers; spec.env of the TriggerAuthentication, rendered verbatim when non-empty.

podIdentity.description: The TriggerAuthentication's spec.podIdentity (e.g. provider: azure-workload), rendered verbatim when non-empty.

hashiCorpVault.description: The TriggerAuthentication's spec.hashiCorpVault, rendered verbatim when non-empty.

azureKeyVault.description: The TriggerAuthentication's spec.azureKeyVault, rendered verbatim when non-empty.

awsSecretManager.description: The TriggerAuthentication's spec.awsSecretManager, rendered verbatim when non-empty.

gcpSecretManager.description: The TriggerAuthentication's spec.gcpSecretManager, rendered verbatim when non-empty.

enabled.description: Renders a policy/v1 PodDisruptionBudget selecting the workload's pods. Exactly one of minAvailable and maxUnavailable is required: the render fails on none or both.

minAvailable.description: A count as an integer, or a percentage from 0% to 100% as a string ("25%"), as the API server requires. A digit string with no percent sign is rejected: spell a count as a number. The render fails when it leaves no pod to evict at the replica owner's floor (replicaCount, autoscaling.minReplicas or keda.minReplicaCount): set maxUnavailable: 0 to block evictions on purpose.

maxUnavailable.description: A count as an integer, or a percentage from 0% to 100% as a string ("25%"), as the API server requires. A digit string with no percent sign is rejected: spell a count as a number.

enabled.description: Render the NetworkPolicy; false when unset. true with none of policyTypes, ingress or egress set fails the render.

policyTypes.description: Rendered verbatim as spec.policyTypes: Ingress, Egress or both. Unset, derived from the ingress and egress set. Listing a type with no rules for it denies all of that traffic.

ingress.description: Ingress rules, rendered verbatim as spec.ingress. Setting it adds Ingress to the policyTypes the chart derives.

from.description: Sources the rule allows; empty or unset, every source.

ports.description: Ports of the workload's pods the rule allows; empty or unset, every port.

egress.description: Egress rules, rendered verbatim as spec.egress. Setting it adds Egress to the policyTypes the chart derives.

to.description: Destinations the rule allows; empty or unset, every destination.

ports.description: Destination ports the rule allows; empty or unset, every port.

networkPolicyPeer.description: A NetworkPolicy v1 peer. Closed in full: a small, fixed shape (ADR 0017).

podSelector.description: Pods the peer selects, rendered verbatim; without namespaceSelector, in the NetworkPolicy's own namespace.

namespaceSelector.description: Namespaces whose pods the peer selects, rendered verbatim; {} selects every namespace. With podSelector in the same peer, only the pods matching both.

ipBlock.description: An IP range, rendered verbatim: cidr, minus the except ranges.

cidr.description: The range allowed, in CIDR notation, such as 10.0.0.0/16.

except.description: CIDR ranges inside cidr left out of it.

networkPolicyPort.description: A NetworkPolicy v1 port. Closed in full: a small, fixed shape (ADR 0017).

protocol.description: TCP (Kubernetes' default when unset), UDP or SCTP.

port.description: A port number or a named container port. Unset, every port of the protocol.

endPort.description: With a numeric port: the last port of the range starting at port.

labelSelector.description: A Kubernetes LabelSelector. Closed in full: a small, fixed shape (ADR 0017).

matchLabels.description: Labels a match must carry, key to value, rendered verbatim.

matchExpressions.description: Set-based requirements, rendered verbatim; every one must match.

key.description: The label key the requirement tests.

values.description: The label values to match. Kubernetes requires a non-empty list for In and NotIn, and none for Exists and DoesNotExist.

nameservers.description: Nameserver IPs, rendered as dnsConfig.nameservers, each quoted.

searches.description: DNS search domains, rendered as dnsConfig.searches, each quoted.

options.description: Resolver options, rendered as dnsConfig.options. An empty dnsConfig, with no nameservers, searches or options, renders no dnsConfig block.

deploymentName.description: Key of the workloads map. It lands raw in the 'app.kubernetes.io/component' label value, as part of the container name, and as '<key>-hook' when the workload has hooks: a DNS-1123 label, capped at 58 so that the '-hook' suffix fits. The cap holds even without hooks, so adding a hook later cannot invalidate a key that was valid.

jobName.description: Key of a cronJobs or hooks.<type> map, at either scope. At workload scope it becomes the container name raw, a DNS-1123 label; the root scope goes through a truncated fullname, but one rule holds for both.

hookType.description: Key of a hooks map: a Helm hook type, lowercase. An unknown type renders and Helm drops the resource with an INFO log and exit 0; at workload scope it also drops the shared prereq ConfigMap/Secret, whose helm.sh/hook joins every type. Helm accepts an uppercase type, but the chart's checks are case-sensitive. 'test-success' is Helm's alias of 'test'.

dns1123Label.description: A DNS-1123 label: lowercase alphanumerics and '-', starting and ending with an alphanumeric. The length bound is the caller's, via maxLength next to the $ref: it depends on what the value is joined to.

portNumberOrName.description: A port as Kubernetes takes it where a number or a name is allowed: 1-65535, or a container port name (IANA_SVC_NAME).

ianaSvcName.description: An IANA_SVC_NAME, as Kubernetes validates a Service port name, a container port name and a named targetPort: at most 15 characters, lowercase alphanumerics and '-', no leading, trailing or doubled '-', and at least one letter. Two patterns under allOf because Go regexp has no lookahead: the first fixes the shape, the second the letter. portName and targetPort also accept "": the API server takes it on a single-port Service (targetPort defaults to port), so it is not rejected here; extraPorts[].name never does, since extra ports make the Service multi-port.

optionalObjectName.description: The name of an existing object, used verbatim: a DNS-1123 subdomain of at most 253 characters, or null / "" for unset. Shared by serviceAccountName and priorityClassName.

dns1123Subdomain.description: A DNS-1123 subdomain: dot-separated DNS-1123 labels. Constrains the keys of the externalSecrets and kedaTriggerAuthentications maps, which become part of a resource name, rbacs.roles[].name, which becomes the Role, RoleBinding and default ServiceAccount names, serviceAccount.name / serviceAccountName in every scope, and nameOverride / fullnameOverride. No maxLength here: the map keys are prefixed by the fullname, which the schema cannot see; the names used verbatim add maxLength 253 at their call site.

mountedConfigFileName.description: Name of a mounted config file entry. Bounded at 52 chars because it feeds the pod volume name 'md-cm-file-<name>', a DNS-1123 label capped at 63. The same bound applies to bundle entries even though 'md-cm-bundle-<i>' has room: one number, taken from the tightest side.

files.description: Mounted config files mounted one by one: each is a ConfigMap <workload fullname>-md-cm-<name>, a volume md-cm-file-<name> and a read-only subPath mount at targetPath in the main container. Its content is in the pod template checksum, so a change replaces the pods.

name.description: Names the ConfigMap, <workload fullname>-md-cm-<name>, and the pod volume, md-cm-file-<name>. A DNS-1123 label of at most 52 characters, unique across files and bundles of the workload.

filename.description: Required. The ConfigMap key and the subPath of the mount, such as app.yaml.

targetPath.description: Required. The full path of the file in the main container, such as /etc/app/app.yaml: the mountPath of its subPath mount. Two mounts on one mountPath fail the render.

content.description: The file's content, rendered verbatim as the ConfigMap value. Required: an absent or null content fails the render; "" is an empty file.

bundles.description: Mounted config files mounted together as one directory: each bundle is a projected volume md-cm-bundle-<index>, mounted read-only at mountDir, with one ConfigMap per file.

mountDir.description: Required. The directory the bundle is mounted at, read-only, in the main container. Two mounts on one mountPath fail the render.

files.description: The bundle's files, each rendered as its own ConfigMap <workload fullname>-md-cm-<name>. Their names share one namespace with files[]: a name used twice fails the render.

name.description: Names the file's ConfigMap, <workload fullname>-md-cm-<name>. A DNS-1123 label of at most 52 characters, unique across files and bundles of the workload.

relPath.description: Required. The file's path under mountDir, such as conf.d/app.conf; its last segment is the ConfigMap key.

content.description: The file's content, rendered verbatim as the ConfigMap value. Required: an absent or null content fails the render; "" is an empty file.

deployment.description: A workload of the release (ADR 0020). strategy and progressDeadlineSeconds apply to a Deployment only; updateStrategy, podManagementPolicy, volumeClaimTemplates and persistentVolumeClaimRetentionPolicy to a StatefulSet only.

enabled.description: false skips the entry and every resource it renders, its hooks and cronjobs included; true when unset. An ingress or route backend naming it fails the render.

kind.description: The workload kind this entry renders as (ADR 0020): Deployment (the default) for interchangeable pods, StatefulSet for pods with a stable identity and claims of their own. Changing it on an installed entry replaces the workload.

replicaCount.description: Pods of the workload; 2 when unset. Ignored, and spec.replicas omitted, while autoscaling or keda owns the replicas.

image.description: Image of the main container: a full reference string, or a map of repository, tag or digest and pullPolicy. Required. Inherited by the workload's hooks and cronjobs unless they set their own.

command.description: Overrides the image ENTRYPOINT of the main container; the image's own when unset. Never inherited by the workload's hooks and cronjobs.

args.description: Overrides the image CMD of the main container; the image's own when unset. Never inherited by the workload's hooks and cronjobs.

imagePullSecrets.description: Pull secrets of the pod; global.imagePullSecrets when unset, and [] renders none. Inherited by the workload's hooks and cronjobs.

serviceAccount.description: The workload's ServiceAccount: created by default, named <fullname>-<key> unless name is set. With create: false, name binds an existing one; with no name, the pod runs as the namespace's default. Inherited by the workload's hooks and cronjobs.

annotations.description: Annotations on the workload's own metadata, merged over global.commonAnnotations. Not podAnnotations, and not propagated to the Service, ServiceAccount, HPA or any other resource of the workload.

podAnnotations.description: Annotations on the pod template, merged over global.commonAnnotations and the annotations the chart adds to roll the pods on a change of a watched source (checksum/config and the like), this one winning.

podLabels.description: Labels on the pod template, merged over global.commonLabels and the chart's own labels, this one winning, except over the selector labels (app.kubernetes.io/name, app.kubernetes.io/instance, app.kubernetes.io/component): a key equal to one of them is dropped, so the template keeps matching the workload's selector.

podSecurityContext.description: The pod's securityContext, rendered verbatim (fsGroup, runAsNonRoot, ...). Inherited by the workload's hooks and cronjobs.

securityContext.description: The main container's securityContext, rendered verbatim (runAsUser, readOnlyRootFilesystem, ...). Inherited by the workload's hooks and cronjobs.

automountServiceAccountToken.description: Pod-level automountServiceAccountToken; omitted when unset, and the ServiceAccount decides. Wins over the ServiceAccount's setting. Inherited by the workload's hooks and cronjobs (ADR 0014).

service.description: The Service in front of the workload, rendered by default: one primary port plus extraPorts. Its ports also declare the main container's ports.

resources.description: Resource requests and limits of the main container, rendered verbatim; none when unset. Not inherited by the workload's hooks and cronjobs, which fall back to defaults.resources.

livenessProbe.description: The main container's liveness probe, rendered verbatim: the kubelet restarts the container when it fails.

readinessProbe.description: The main container's readiness probe, rendered verbatim: the pod receives Service traffic only while it passes.

startupProbe.description: The main container's startup probe, rendered verbatim: liveness and readiness probes wait until it passes once.

lifecycle.description: The main container's lifecycle hooks (postStart, preStop), rendered verbatim: a preStop sleep gives endpoints time to drop the pod.

terminationGracePeriodSeconds.description: Seconds between SIGTERM and SIGKILL on pod shutdown. Kubernetes defaults to 30.

autoscaling.description: A HorizontalPodAutoscaler for the workload. With enabled: true it owns the replicas: spec.replicas is omitted. Excludes keda.

keda.description: A KEDA ScaledObject for the workload; KEDA creates and owns its own HPA. With enabled: true it owns the replicas: spec.replicas is omitted. Excludes autoscaling. Needs the keda.sh CRDs.

reloader.description: Opt-in Stakater Reloader annotations on the workload's metadata (ADR 0016).

strategy.description: Deployment only: spec.strategy, rendered verbatim (type RollingUpdate with maxSurge and maxUnavailable, or Recreate).

revisionHistoryLimit.description: Old revisions kept for rollback: ReplicaSets for a Deployment, ControllerRevisions for a StatefulSet. Kubernetes defaults to 10.

progressDeadlineSeconds.description: Deployment only: seconds a rollout may go without progress before Kubernetes marks it failed. Kubernetes defaults to 600.

updateStrategy.description: StatefulSet only: RollingUpdate, with an optional partition, or OnDelete.

podManagementPolicy.description: StatefulSet only: OrderedReady (the Kubernetes default) starts and stops the pods one at a time, in ordinal order; Parallel does not wait. Immutable once the StatefulSet exists.

volumeClaimTemplates.description: StatefulSet only: one claim per pod for each entry, named <name>-<statefulset>-<ordinal>, which follows the pod across restarts. Every entry must be mounted by a volumeMounts item. Immutable once the StatefulSet exists (ADR 0020).

persistentVolumeClaimRetentionPolicy.description: StatefulSet only: whether the claims are kept or deleted when the StatefulSet is deleted or scaled down. Both default to Retain.

topologySpreadConstraints.description: The pod's topologySpreadConstraints, rendered verbatim: its labelSelector is not filled in, so name the selector labels yourself.

pdb.description: A PodDisruptionBudget for the workload, rendered when enabled.

networkPolicy.description: A NetworkPolicy selecting the workload's pods, rendered when enabled.

volumes.description: The pod's volumes, each a native volume source. Not inherited by the workload's hooks and cronjobs.

volumeMounts.description: The main container's volumeMounts. Not inherited by the workload's hooks and cronjobs.

nodeSelector.description: The pod's nodeSelector. Inherited by the workload's hooks and cronjobs.

priorityClassName.description: Name of an existing PriorityClass for the pod (a DNS-1123 subdomain, at most 253 characters). The PriorityClass itself is cluster-scoped and not rendered by the chart. Inherited by the workload's hooks and cronjobs; null or "" means unset.

tolerations.description: The pod's tolerations. Inherited by the workload's hooks and cronjobs.

affinity.description: The pod's affinity, rendered verbatim (nodeAffinity, podAffinity, podAntiAffinity). Inherited by the workload's hooks and cronjobs.

secret.description: Key/value pairs of a Secret named <fullname>-<key>, base64-encoded by the chart, read by the main container as an envFrom source. A change rolls the pods. Inherited by the workload's hooks and cronjobs unless they set inheritWorkloadSecret: false.

configMap.description: Key/value pairs of a ConfigMap named <fullname>-<key>, read by the main container as an envFrom source. A change rolls the pods. Inherited by the workload's hooks and cronjobs unless they set inheritWorkloadConfigMap: false.

hostAliases.description: The pod's hostAliases: extra /etc/hosts entries. Inherited by the workload's hooks and cronjobs.

dnsConfig.description: The pod's dnsConfig (nameservers, searches, options). Inherited by the workload's cronjobs, not by its hooks.

envFromConfigMaps.description: Names of existing ConfigMaps the main container reads as envFrom sources. Inherited by the workload's hooks and cronjobs, read before their own, unless they set inheritWorkloadEnvFromConfigMaps: false.

envFromSecrets.description: Names of existing Secrets the main container reads as envFrom sources. Inherited by the workload's hooks and cronjobs, read before their own, unless they set inheritWorkloadEnvFromSecrets: false. For a Secret the release's own ExternalSecret produces, use externalSecrets.

externalSecrets.description: Secrets of the root externalSecrets map, by key: an envFrom source, or a read-only volume with mountPath. Inherited by the workload's hooks and cronjobs; a job's own list, [] included, replaces it.

additionalEnvs.description: Environment variables of the main container. Inherited by the workload's hooks and cronjobs, before their own env.

extraInitContainers.description: Init containers of the pod, rendered verbatim.

extraContainers.description: Sidecar containers of the pod, after the main container, rendered verbatim.

podRecreation.description: Roll the pods on every render.

enabled.description: true adds a timestamp annotation to the pod template, so every helm upgrade rolls the pods: with pullPolicy: Always, a moved tag is pulled again. A change to configMap, secret, mountedConfigFiles, or the spec of a referenced externalSecrets entry, rolls the pods without it.

mountedConfigFiles.description: Files the chart renders as ConfigMaps and mounts into the main container. Never inherited by the workload's hooks and cronjobs.

hooks.description: Workload-scope Helm hooks: hooks.<hook type>.<name>, each a Job run at that phase. They inherit the workload's image, serviceAccount, configMap, secret, envFromConfigMaps, envFromSecrets, externalSecrets, additionalEnvs, imagePullSecrets, hostAliases, podSecurityContext, securityContext, automountServiceAccountToken, nodeSelector, tolerations, affinity and priorityClassName; never command, args, mountedConfigFiles, volumes, volumeMounts or resources.

cronJobs.description: Workload-scope CronJobs keyed by name. They inherit the workload's image, serviceAccount, configMap, secret, envFromConfigMaps, envFromSecrets, externalSecrets, additionalEnvs, imagePullSecrets, hostAliases, podSecurityContext, securityContext, automountServiceAccountToken, nodeSelector, tolerations, affinity, priorityClassName and dnsConfig; never command, args, mountedConfigFiles, volumes, volumeMounts or resources.

statefulSetUpdateStrategy.description: StatefulSet only. Closed: a small, fixed shape (ADR 0017). rollingUpdate.maxUnavailable is left out: it is alpha. rollingUpdate is rejected with type OnDelete, as the API server does.

type.description: RollingUpdate replaces the pods one at a time, highest ordinal first; OnDelete replaces a pod only when it is deleted. Unset, left out, and Kubernetes defaults to RollingUpdate.

rollingUpdate.description: Only with type RollingUpdate: partition, the lowest ordinal the rollout updates.

partition.description: Only the pods with an ordinal at or above it are updated.

persistentVolumeClaimRetentionPolicy.description: StatefulSet only: what happens to the claims when the StatefulSet is deleted or scaled down. Both default to Retain, so an uninstall, a prune or a scale-down keeps the data. Delete removes the claim, and with a Delete reclaim policy its volume.

whenDeleted.description: The claims' fate when the StatefulSet is deleted; Retain when unset.

whenScaled.description: The fate of the claims of the pods a scale-down removes; Retain when unset.

volumeClaimTemplate.description: One StatefulSet claim template. Closed: a small, fixed shape (ADR 0017). Its metadata carries the selector labels and its own labels and annotations only, never the chart's or the common ones: the template is immutable, and a label that changes with the chart version would make every upgrade a forbidden update.

name.description: The pod volume name a volumeMounts item mounts, and the head of each claim's name.

size.description: Requested storage: a positive Kubernetes quantity, such as 10Gi.

storageClassName.description: Absent takes the cluster's default StorageClass; "" asks for no dynamic provisioning. A cloud block disk lives in one zone: a class with volumeBindingMode: WaitForFirstConsumer creates it in the zone of the pod's node.

labels.description: Labels on each claim, under the workload's selector labels, which win on a shared key. global.commonLabels is not added.

annotations.description: Annotations on each claim, rendered verbatim; global.commonAnnotations is not added.

image.description: Image of the job: a full reference string, or a map of repository, tag or digest and pullPolicy. Workload scope: the workload's when unset. Root scope: required, unless fromWorkload is set.

command.description: Overrides the image ENTRYPOINT; the image's own when unset. Never inherited from the workload.

args.description: Overrides the image CMD; the image's own when unset. Never inherited from the workload.

resources.description: Resource requests and limits of the job's container; defaults.resources when unset, and {} renders none. Never inherited from the workload.

serviceAccount.description: The job's ServiceAccount. Its name: serviceAccountName or serviceAccount.name, else the workload's ServiceAccount, else one the chart creates under the job's name. create: false with nothing named leaves the pod on the namespace default. A hook may run as a hook-prerequisite copy of it (ADR 0011).

serviceAccountName.description: Existing ServiceAccount the job runs as. Same rule as serviceAccount.name: a DNS-1123 subdomain of at most 253 characters; null or "" means unset.

serviceAccountAnnotations.description: Annotations on the ServiceAccount the job creates, when serviceAccount.annotations is unset.

imagePullPolicy.description: Overrides the pull policy; else the pullPolicy of the image the job runs, inherited one included, else IfNotPresent.

imagePullSecrets.description: Pull secrets of the job's pod. Workload scope: the workload's when unset, then global.imagePullSecrets. Root scope: global.imagePullSecrets. [] renders none.

nodeSelector.description: The pod's nodeSelector. Workload scope: the workload's when unset; {} stops the inheritance.

priorityClassName.description: Name of an existing PriorityClass for the job pod. Workload scope: explicit > inherited from the workload. "" stops the inheritance; null is unset, so the workload's value is inherited. Root scope: only this value.

tolerations.description: The pod's tolerations. Workload scope: the workload's when unset; [] stops the inheritance.

affinity.description: The pod's affinity, rendered verbatim. Workload scope: the workload's when unset; {} stops the inheritance.

hostAliases.description: The pod's hostAliases. Workload scope: the workload's when unset; [] stops the inheritance.

dnsConfig.description: The pod's dnsConfig. A workload-scope cronjob takes the workload's when unset; a hook never inherits it.

env.description: Environment variables of the job's container. Workload scope: added after the workload's additionalEnvs.

envFromConfigMaps.description: Names of existing ConfigMaps read as envFrom sources. Workload scope: added after the workload's envFromConfigMaps, never replacing them.

envFromSecrets.description: Names of existing Secrets read as envFrom sources. Workload scope: added after the workload's envFromSecrets, never replacing them.

externalSecrets.description: Secrets of the root externalSecrets map, by key: an envFrom source, or a read-only volume with mountPath. Workload scope: replaces the workload's list, [] included. A pre-* hook (pre-delete excepted) and a post-delete hook read the hook-prerequisite copy (ADR 0007).

annotations.description: Annotations on the CronJob, or on the hook's Job, merged over global.commonAnnotations.

automountServiceAccountToken.description: Pod-level automountServiceAccountToken. Workload scope: the workload's when unset; else omitted, and the ServiceAccount decides (ADR 0014).

volumes.description: The job pod's volumes, each a native volume source. The job's own: never inherited from the workload.

volumeMounts.description: The job container's volumeMounts. The job's own: never inherited from the workload.

restartPolicy.description: The pod's restartPolicy: Never (the default) or OnFailure.

podSecurityContext.description: The pod's securityContext, rendered verbatim. Workload scope: the workload's when unset; {} stops the inheritance.

securityContext.description: The container's securityContext, rendered verbatim. Workload scope: the workload's when unset; {} stops the inheritance.

schedule.description: Cron schedule in the five-field format, such as "0 2 * * *".

initContainers.description: Init containers of the job's pod, rendered verbatim. CronJobs only.

backoffLimit.description: Retries before a Job is marked failed. Kubernetes defaults to 6.

ttlSecondsAfterFinished.description: Seconds after a Job finishes before Kubernetes deletes it.

activeDeadlineSeconds.description: Bound on a Job's run time: its pods are stopped and the Job marked failed past it.

startingDeadlineSeconds.description: Seconds after a missed schedule within which the run may still start; unset, no deadline.

parallelism.description: Pods of a Job running at once.

completions.description: Successful pods a Job needs to complete.

timeZone.description: Time zone of the schedule, an IANA name such as Europe/Rome; the controller manager's when unset.

suspend.description: true stops new runs without removing the CronJob; running Jobs are left alone.

concurrencyPolicy.description: Forbid (the default) skips a run while the previous one is active; Allow runs them side by side; Replace stops the previous one.

weight.description: Hook weight. A string holds a plain integer: a leading zero is rejected, since the weight arithmetic would read "010" as octal 8.

deletePolicy.description: helm.sh/hook-delete-policy of the hook's Job and of the ServiceAccount it creates. Unset: before-hook-creation on the Job, so the last run stays as the record of what ran; before-hook-creation,hook-succeeded,hook-failed on the ServiceAccount.

activeDeadlineSeconds.description: Bound on the hook Job's run time. The only bound on a hook pod that waits for a Secret: it never reaches Failed, so backoffLimit never counts it.

backoffLimit.description: Retries before the hook Job is marked failed; Kubernetes defaults to 6. The hook's own: no fallback from the workload or global. Why the other Job spec fields are not offered on a hook: see jobSpecVerbatimFields in _job-helpers.tpl.

fromWorkload.description: Key of a workload whose image, with its pullPolicy, the job runs; a key naming no workload fails the render. Ignored when the job sets image. Nothing else is inherited.

inheritWorkloadConfigMap.description: false drops the workload's generated ConfigMap (configMap) from this job's envFrom. Default true.

inheritWorkloadSecret.description: false drops the workload's generated Secret (secret) from this job's envFrom. Default true.

inheritWorkloadEnvFromConfigMaps.description: false drops the workload's envFromConfigMaps from this job's envFrom. Default true.

inheritWorkloadEnvFromSecrets.description: false drops the workload's envFromSecrets from this job's envFrom. Default true. externalSecrets have their own rule: a job's own list replaces the inherited one.

key.description: The key in the external store, rendered as remoteRef.key. Required: a render fail names the remote when it is missing.

conversionStrategy.description: ESO's remoteRef.conversionStrategy (Default or Unicode); Default when unset.

decodingStrategy.description: ESO's remoteRef.decodingStrategy (None, Base64, Base64URL or Auto); None when unset.

metadataPolicy.description: ESO's remoteRef.metadataPolicy (None or Fetch); None when unset.

property.description: The property of a structured remote value to read, rendered as remoteRef.property. Rendered only when set, "" included; no chart default.

version.description: The version of the remote value, rendered as remoteRef.version, a quoted string: version: 3 is accepted. Rendered only when set; no chart default.

externalSecretRef.description: A reference to a key of the root externalSecrets map, never to the Secret it produces. Without mountPath the Secret is an envFrom source; with it, a read-only volume mounted there. A pre-* hook other than pre-delete, and a post-delete hook, read the Secret of the hook-prerequisite copy (ADR 0007).

name.description: A key of the root externalSecrets map. A key that is missing or whose entry is empty is a render fail.

mountPath.description: Mount the Secret as a read-only volume at this path instead of injecting it as an envFrom source. The volume name derives from the key, which must then make a DNS-1123 label of at most 63 characters; mounting the same key twice, or a path another mount uses, is a render fail.

annotations.description: Annotations on the ExternalSecret, merged over global.commonAnnotations. Not copied onto its hook-prerequisite copy, which is ordered by hook phase (ADR 0007).

remote.description: Single-key form: where the one key lives in the store, rendered as spec.data[0].remoteRef. Required, with secretkey, unless data or dataFrom is set; it cannot be combined with them (render fail).

data.description: Several keys from the store: each item becomes an entry of spec.data. Combines with dataFrom, not with the single-key remote / secretkey (render fail).

secretkey.description: The key of the produced Secret that receives the value, rendered as the item's secretKey. Required: a render fail names the item when it is missing.

remote.description: Where the key lives in the store, rendered as the item's remoteRef. Required: a render fail names the item when it is missing.

dataFrom.description: ESO's spec.dataFrom, rendered verbatim: each item fetches many keys at once (extract, find) or from a generator. Combines with data, not with the single-key remote / secretkey (render fail).

extract.description: ESO's dataFrom[].extract, rendered verbatim: every property of one remote key becomes a key of the Secret.

find.description: ESO's dataFrom[].find, rendered verbatim: every remote key matching its name or tags becomes a key of the Secret.

rewrite.description: ESO's dataFrom[].rewrite, rendered verbatim: the rules that rename the fetched keys before they land in the Secret.

sourceRef.description: A per-entry source. Closed in full: ESO adds generator types, not fields to the reference (ADR 0017). No enum on the kinds.

storeRef.description: A store for this entry alone, rendered verbatim as ESO's sourceRef.storeRef; it overrides secretstore for the entry.

name.description: The name of the store. Required.

kind.description: SecretStore or ClusterSecretStore. Rendered only when set; ESO's default applies otherwise.

generatorRef.description: A generator the entry draws from instead of a store, rendered verbatim as ESO's sourceRef.generatorRef.

apiVersion.description: The generator's apiVersion. Rendered only when set; ESO's default applies otherwise.

kind.description: The generator's kind, such as Password or ECRAuthorizationToken. Required.

name.description: The name of the generator resource. Required.

secretstore.description: The store the entry reads from, rendered as spec.secretStoreRef. Required, with both kind and name, unless the entry has only dataFrom and every item carries its own sourceRef.

kind.description: SecretStore or ClusterSecretStore. Required whenever secretstore is rendered.

name.description: The name of the store. Required whenever secretstore is rendered.

secretkey.description: Single-key form: the key of the produced Secret that receives the value of remote, rendered as spec.data[0].secretKey. Required, with remote, unless data or dataFrom is set; it cannot be combined with them (render fail).

refreshInterval.description: ESO's spec.refreshInterval, a duration such as 1h or 15m; 1h when unset.

target.description: ESO's spec.target: the Secret the ExternalSecret produces and how it is written.

creationPolicy.description: ESO's target.creationPolicy; Owner when unset. CreateOrMerge needs an ESO release that ships it.

deletionPolicy.description: ESO's target.deletionPolicy: what happens to the Secret's data when the remote keys are gone. Retain when unset.

name.description: The name of the produced Secret; <fullname>-<key> when unset. The hook-prerequisite copy produces <name>-hook (ADR 0007). A render fail catches a target that lands on another ExternalSecret's or on a Secret the chart renders (ADR 0013).

immutable.description: ESO's target.immutable, rendered only when set: the produced Secret cannot change once written. A workload's checksum/external-secrets does not cover the new data of an immutable Secret.

template.description: ESO's target.template, rendered verbatim: the shape of the produced Secret (type, metadata, data built from the fetched keys).

enabled.description: Render the Ingress; false when unset. true together with httpRoute.enabled or any httpRoutes entry fails the render: one HTTP routing layer per release.

className.description: Rendered as spec.ingressClassName; "" leaves it out, so the cluster's default IngressClass applies. The chart's values.yaml sets nginx.

annotations.description: Annotations on the Ingress, merged over global.commonAnnotations.

tls.description: spec.tls of the Ingress: one entry per certificate.

hosts.description: Hosts the certificate covers, rendered as the entry's hosts.

secretName.description: The TLS Secret holding the certificate and key for those hosts, in the release namespace. The chart does not create it.

hosts.description: One Ingress rule per entry, each routed to one backend: a workload's Service, or service.name. The template does not require an entry: with none, the Ingress carries no rules and Kubernetes rejects it.

host.description: The rule's host, such as api.example.com. Unset, the rule matches every host.

workload.description: The workload whose Service the rule routes to, unless service.name is set. A workload that does not exist, is empty, has enabled: false or service.enabled: false fails the render, as does an entry with neither workload nor service.name.

portName.description: With workload: the name of the Service port to route to, service.portName or a service.extraPorts[].name; omitted, the primary port. The port must be TCP. Rejected together with a service name or port.

service.description: An explicit Service backend, in place of workload: name, and port (80 when unset). A service.name wins over workload.

paths.description: The rule's paths, at least one, all routed to the entry's backend.

path.description: The path to match, such as /, rendered verbatim.

pathType.description: Exact, Prefix or ImplementationSpecific; ImplementationSpecific when unset.

httpRoute.description: The single HTTPRoute, named <fullname>, rendered when enabled. Its fields are httpRouteFields', shared with an httpRoutes entry.

enabled.description: Renders the single HTTPRoute, named <fullname>. Default false. Enabled, parentRefs and rules must each hold at least one entry, or the render fails; it excludes ingress, since both are the HTTP routing layer.

httpRouteFields.description: The fields of an HTTPRoute the chart renders, shared by httpRoute and an httpRoutes entry (issue #195). An allOf branch: never closed; the two that reference it are, through unevaluatedProperties (Helm >= 3.18.6).

annotations.description: Annotations of the HTTPRoute, merged with global.commonAnnotations, this one winning.

parentRefs.description: The existing Gateways the HTTPRoute attaches to, rendered verbatim as spec.parentRefs. At least one, or the render fails.

hostnames.description: Hostnames the HTTPRoute answers, rendered as spec.hostnames. Unset or empty, the field is omitted and the route matches every hostname of its listener.

rules.description: The routing rules, rendered as spec.rules. At least one, or the render fails.

httpRouteEntry.description: An httpRoutes entry: one HTTPRoute named <fullname>-<key> (issue #195), with httpRouteFields' fields. An entry present is a route rendered, so parentRefs and rules are required.

parentRefs.description: The Gateways the route attaches to. Required, at least one.

rules.description: The routing rules. Required, at least one.

matches.description: Conditions a request must meet to take this rule, rendered verbatim as rules[].matches. Unset, the Gateway API default applies: every path.

path.description: Path match, rendered verbatim. Its defaults are the Gateway API's, not the chart's.

type.description: Exact, PathPrefix or RegularExpression. Unset, the Gateway API default applies (PathPrefix).

value.description: Path to match. Unset, the Gateway API default applies (/).

headers.description: Header matches, rendered verbatim. A request must carry them all.

type.description: Exact or RegularExpression. Unset, the Gateway API default applies (Exact).

name.description: Header name, matched case-insensitively.

value.description: Value to match the header against.

queryParams.description: Query parameter matches, rendered verbatim. A request must carry them all.

type.description: Exact or RegularExpression. Unset, the Gateway API default applies (Exact).

name.description: Query parameter name, matched exactly.

value.description: Value to match the query parameter against.

method.description: HTTP method to match, rendered verbatim. Unset, every method.

filters.description: Gateway API filters of the rule, rendered verbatim as rules[].filters. Only type is checked; the other fields of a filter pass through. A RequestRedirect makes the rule one without backendRefs.

type.description: The Gateway API filter type. Required, a null item is rejected at render time.

backendRefs.description: The backends of the rule, each resolved by resolveBackend to a Service name and port. Required unless filters holds a RequestRedirect, and rejected with one: a redirect answers the request itself.

timeouts.description: Timeouts of the rule, rendered verbatim as rules[].timeouts. Unset, the Gateway implementation's.

request.description: Gateway API Duration, such as 30s: the most the Gateway may take to answer the client, retries included. Rendered verbatim.

backendRequest.description: Gateway API Duration, such as 10s: the most one request to a backend may take. Rendered verbatim.

gatewayParentRef.description: A Gateway API parentRef, rendered verbatim: the Gateway (and optionally its listener) a route attaches to. Shared by httpRoute and the L4 routes.

name.description: Name of the existing Gateway the route attaches to, rendered verbatim. The chart does not create Gateways.

namespace.description: Namespace of the Gateway, rendered verbatim. Unset, the route's own namespace.

sectionName.description: Name of the Gateway listener to attach to, rendered verbatim. Unset, every listener that accepts the route.

port.description: Port of the Gateway listener to attach to, rendered verbatim.

kind.description: Kind of the parent, rendered verbatim. Unset, the Gateway API default applies (Gateway).

group.description: API group of the parent, rendered verbatim. Unset, the Gateway API default applies (gateway.networking.k8s.io).

backendServiceRef.description: An explicit Service backend, in place of a workload: its name and port (default 80). Shared by ingress, httpRoute and the L4 routes.

name.description: Name of the Service, in the release namespace, rendered as the backendRef or Ingress backend name. Set, it takes precedence over workload; empty, it counts as unset.

port.description: Port of the Service to reach. Default 80, not the primary port of a workload: the chart cannot see a Service it does not create.

backendPortName.description: With workload: the name of the port of the workload's Service to route to, service.portName or a service.extraPorts[].name (issue #194). Omitted, the primary port. Its protocol must be the one the route forwards; rejected together with service, at render time.

l4Route.description: A TCPRoute or UDPRoute (gateway.networking.k8s.io/v1, Gateway API v1.6.0 or later), named <fullname>-<key>. An entry present is a route rendered.

annotations.description: Annotations of the route, merged with global.commonAnnotations, this one winning.

parentRefs.description: The existing Gateway listeners the route attaches to, rendered verbatim as spec.parentRefs. Required, at least one.

rules.description: The rules of the route, rendered as spec.rules. Required, at least one.

name.description: Name of the rule, rendered as rules[].name. Unset, omitted.

backendRefs.description: The backends of the rule, each resolved by resolveBackend to a Service name and port. Required, at least one; the port must carry the route's protocol, TCP for tcpRoutes and UDP for udpRoutes.

httpRouteBackendRef.description: A backendRef of httpRoute: routeBackendRef's fields plus filters. Its own closed $defs rather than an extension, since a closed $defs cannot be extended through allOf.

workload.description: Name of a workloads entry: resolves to its Service, <fullname>-<name>, and the port portName picks. The render fails if the workload does not exist, is empty, or has enabled or service.enabled false.

portName.description: With workload: the name of the workload Service port to route to; omitted, the primary port. Must be a TCP port.

service.description: An explicit Service backend {name, port}, in place of workload. Set with a name, it takes precedence over workload; rejected together with portName.

weight.description: Share of the rule's traffic sent to this backend, relative to the others, rendered as backendRefs[].weight when set. Unset, the Gateway API default applies (1).

filters.description: Gateway API filters applied to this backend only, rendered verbatim as backendRefs[].filters. Only type is checked; the other fields of a filter pass through.

type.description: The Gateway API filter type. Required, a null item is rejected at render time.

routeBackendRef.description: A backendRef of an L4 route: workload (with an optional portName) or service, and an optional weight. Resolved by resolveBackend, like every backend of the chart.

workload.description: Name of a workloads entry: resolves to its Service, <fullname>-<name>, and the port portName picks. The render fails if the workload does not exist, is empty, or has enabled or service.enabled false.

portName.description: With workload: the name of the workload Service port to route to; omitted, the primary port. Its protocol must be the route's.

service.description: An explicit Service backend {name, port}, in place of workload. Set with a name, it takes precedence over workload; rejected together with portName.

weight.description: Share of the rule's traffic sent to this backend, relative to the others, rendered as backendRefs[].weight when set. Unset, the Gateway API default applies (1).

resources.description: Resources of a hook or cronjob that sets no resources key of its own. A job's resources: {} renders none; a workload's resources never reach its jobs.

roles.description: One Role per entry, bound to the entry's ServiceAccount by a RoleBinding when it declares one. A hook running as that ServiceAccount gets a hook-prerequisite copy of the Role and RoleBinding (ADR 0010).

name.description: The Role's name, used verbatim. The RoleBinding is <name>-rolebinding, a trailing -role dropped, and the default ServiceAccount <name>-sa, both truncated to 63 characters; a name landing on another the chart renders is a render fail.

serviceAccount.description: The ServiceAccount the Role is bound to, created as <name>-sa by default; {} is enough to declare it. With create: false it binds an existing one, <name>-sa unless name is set. Without this key no ServiceAccount and no RoleBinding are rendered.

rules.description: The Role's PolicyRules, rendered verbatim; the hook-prerequisite copy grants the same ones.
